facts.statement: The study shows that fruit fly circadian systems use a protein quality control mechanism to maintain daily activity cycles.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Blocking specific quality control proteins in the brain cells that control the body clock disrupted the flies' natural movement patterns.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Removing the protein Caliban, which helps remove defective proteins, caused the adult flies to have weaker and longer daily activity cycles.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The changes in movement were linked to a slower build-up of a key clock protein called PERIOD.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Having one copy of the per gene made the lengthening of the daily cycle worse, while adding more of the TIMELESS protein reduced this effect.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: In lab-grown fly cells lacking Caliban, more incomplete versions of the PERIOD protein were produced.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: The results suggest that the PERIOD protein is a target of this quality control system, linking protein production checks to the timing of the body clock.
facts.subject: animals
